symptoms: Dark brown-black spots with concentric rings (target pattern) on lower leaves
Spots may have yellow halos
Starts on older/lower leaves and moves upward
Premature leaf drop and defoliation
Dark, sunken lesions on stems near soil line
Fruit may develop dark, leathery spots near stem end
cause: Fungus Alternaria solani, spread through wind, rain splash, and infected plant debris. Thrives in warm (24-29°C), humid weather with alternating wet-dry conditions.
treatment: Apply Mancozeb 75% WP at 2.5g/litre water — spray every 10-14 days
Alternatively use Chlorothalonil 75% WP at 2g/litre
Remove and destroy affected lower leaves immediately
Stake plants for better air circulation
Water at soil level, avoid wetting foliage
Apply mulch around base to prevent soil splash
prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds from trusted sources
Maintain 60cm spacing between plants
3-year crop rotation — avoid planting tomato/potato/brinjal in same field
Destroy crop debris after harvest — do not compost infected material
Apply preventive fungicide spray before monsoon season
Use resistant varieties when available

symptoms: Large, irregular, water-soaked greenish-black lesions on leaves
White fuzzy mold on leaf undersides in humid conditions
Rapid browning and death of entire leaves and stems
Firm, dark, greasy-looking spots on green and ripe fruit
Entire plant can collapse within 5-7 days
Strong musty odor from severely affected plants
cause: Oomycete Phytophthora infestans — same pathogen as Irish Potato Famine. Spread by wind-blown sporangia. Requires cool (15-22°C) and wet conditions. Can travel miles through wind.
treatment: URGENT: Apply Copper Oxychloride 50% WP at 3g/litre immediately
Or Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold) at 2.5g/litre
Spray ENTIRE field including unaffected plants
Remove and BURN infected plants — DO NOT compost
Avoid any overhead irrigation
Contact nearest KVK for emergency guidance
prevention: Plant resistant varieties (Check PAU/IARI recommendations)
Never plant near potato fields
Ensure excellent air flow — stake and prune plants
Avoid overhead irrigation
Scout fields daily during cool, wet weather
Destroy all volunteer tomato and potato plants

symptoms: Pale greenish-yellow spots on upper leaf surface
Velvety olive-green to brown mold on leaf undersides
Lower and middle leaves affected first
Leaves may curl, wither, and drop
Rarely affects fruit but reduces overall yield
cause: Fungus Passalora fulva (syn. Cladosporium fulvum). Thrives in high humidity (>85%) and warm greenhouse/polyhouse conditions. Spores persist on plant debris and structures.
treatment: Improve ventilation — open polyhouse vents daily
Apply Chlorothalonil 75% WP at 2g/litre
Reduce humidity below 85%
Remove lower leaves for better air flow
Space plants wider to improve ventilation
prevention: Use resistant varieties
Maintain good ventilation in protected cultivation
Avoid leaf wetness — use drip irrigation
Remove and destroy crop debris between seasons
Sanitize polyhouse structures between crops

symptoms: Small circular spots (2-3mm) with dark borders and grey-white centers
Tiny black dots (pycnidia) visible in spot centers
Starts on lower leaves near soil
Heavy infection causes yellowing and defoliation
Rarely affects fruit directly but reduces quality through defoliation
cause: Fungus Septoria lycopersici. Spread via rain splash from infected debris. Favored by warm (20-25°C), wet weather with extended leaf wetness.
treatment: Apply Mancozeb 75% WP at 2.5g/litre
Or Chlorothalonil at 2g/litre
Remove infected lower leaves promptly
Mulch around plants to prevent soil splash
Water at soil level only
prevention: 3-year crop rotation away from solanaceous crops
Destroy all crop debris after harvest
Use stake support and avoid crowding
Apply mulch to prevent rain-splashed soil
Scout and remove infected leaves early
